issues.description: The template declares singFarmSongVerse with no Animal parameter (private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)) while the solution implements singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) (and with protected visibility). This makes the intended method signature unclear to students: they may implement a private, parameterless helper as in the template, but the tests or reference solution expect a version that accepts an Animal. The mismatch in signature (and accompanying visibility difference: template private vs solution protected) can cause compilation or test-access issues and confusion about how verses should be generated per animal.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template's singFarmSongVerse signature match the intended/solution signature. Update template Farm.java to declare singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) (and consider using protected if tests need access) instead of a parameterless/private version. Alternatively, adjust the solution/tests and problem UML to accept a private, parameterless helper and document how singFarmSong() should call it. Ensure the problem statement/UML and template use the same visibility and parameter list.
